title: Abba Mari the Exilarch
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He is mentioned in [Niddah 67b](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.67b.18): his wife was angry with him and did not want to go to immersion, and Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak went to appease her. Seder Olam Zuta says that he was the son of Mar Ukva the Exilarch, and that Rava and Ravina were his sages; Hyman criticizes all its words as fragmentary, corrupt and incomplete. [Seder HaDorot](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=2404&lang=en) cites from the Maharshal’s responsum 6 that Rav Nachman was his son-in-law; Hyman says, with apologies to his holy bones, that the author thought that Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak was the son-in-law of the Patriarch’s house, as he understood Rashi. Hyman refers to his earlier explanation in the entry Rav Nachman that Rashi’s view too is that Rav Nachman bar Yaakov, not Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak, was the son-in-law of the Patriarch’s house.[^1][^2]

notes.text: Hyman reads סע״ז as Seder Olam Zuta. The genealogy and the criticism of that work belong to his discussion.

The linked Niddah names Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak as the man who went to appease Abba Mari’s wife. In the quotation that Heilprin attributes to Maharshal, the conciliator is called “Rav Nachman, his son-in-law.” Hyman discusses which Rav Nachman was connected by marriage to the Patriarch’s household.
